title: Same hill, new neighbours

cast.B_JOHN: a Romano-British farmer (prologue, invented portrait cast/B_JOHN_ironage.jpg aged on)
cast.A_MARY: a Romano-British farm woman (prologue, invented portrait cast/A_MARY_ironage.jpg)

shots.direction: HOOK (0-5 s): talking close-up of Nia at the reading-room table, looking up from a closed folder; she asks the scene's question straight to camera.

lines.en: Bore da. Same hill, a few hundred years on. Who was farming it, and what was on their minds?
lines.cy: Bore da. Yr un bryn, ychydig gannoedd o flynyddoedd yn ddiweddarach. Pwy oedd yn ei ffermio, a beth oedd ar eu meddwl?
lines.es: Bore da. La misma colina, unos siglos después. ¿Quién la cultivaba y qué les preocupaba?

shots.direction: Wordless wide (5 s): the hilltop fields at harvest, smoke from an unseen hearth beyond the hedge, the Ely marsh and the distant estuary below. Era card in post: 'Second to fourth century AD. Spoken in modern Welsh, the nearest living descendant of the Brittonic language of the time.'

shots.direction: Wordless moving wide (6 s): oxen draw a cart along the field edge, swallows low over the spelt, the Ely marsh below.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal late-summer hilltop farmland in south-east Wales in the Roman period (2nd-3rd century AD): small hedged fields of ripe spelt, a beaten-earth threshing floor, wooden hurdles, oxen, a few cattle and geese; below, the Ely river winding through wide green marsh to a distant silver estuary far away; no sea at the hill's foot; no buildings in frame except a low timber-and-thatch barn edge; no villa, no stone walls, no tiled roofs, no mosaics, no text, no heraldry

shots.direction: Talking close-up of the farmer at the threshing floor, rubbing an ear of spelt between his palms.

lines.en: Good spelt this year. Dry enough to thresh before the rain comes up the valley.
lines.cy: Sbelt da eleni. Digon sych i'w ddyrnu cyn i'r glaw ddod i fyny'r cwm.
lines.es: Buena espelta este año. Lo bastante seca para trillarla antes de que la lluvia suba por el valle.

shots.direction: Talking close-up of the farm woman kneeling at a rotary quern, grain in her lap.

lines.en: Then thresh it quick. The quern's hungry, and so are the children.
lines.cy: Dyrna fe'n glou, 'te. Mae'r maen breuan yn llwglyd, a'r plant hefyd.
lines.es: Pues trilla rápido. El molino de mano tiene hambre, y los niños también.

shots.direction: Moving two-shot: the pair load sacks onto an ox cart at the field gate; a track runs down toward the river. The farmer's line plays as he talks while working (no face close-up).

lines.en: The soldiers' buyers are at the river ford tomorrow. They pay for the grain in salt and good red pots.
lines.cy: Bydd prynwyr y milwyr wrth y rhyd yfory. Maen nhw'n talu am y grawn mewn halen a photiau coch da.
lines.es: Los compradores de los soldados estarán en el vado mañana. Pagan el grano con sal y buenas vasijas rojas.

shots.direction: Talking close-up of the farm woman holding up a glossy red bowl, amused.

lines.en: Pots from far away, and we still eat the same porridge out of them.
lines.cy: Potiau o bell, ac rydyn ni'n dal i fwyta'r un uwd ohonyn nhw.
lines.es: Vasijas de muy lejos, y seguimos comiendo las mismas gachas en ellas.

shots.direction: Talking close-up of the farmer, glancing across the field to a low bump in the grass.

lines.en: Mam's mother used to say her people kept a round house right here. Now it's the barn and the oxen.
lines.cy: Roedd mam Mam yn arfer dweud bod ei phobl hi'n cadw tŷ crwn yn union fan hyn. Nawr, yr ysgubor a'r ychen sydd yma.
lines.es: La madre de mamá decía que su gente tenía una casa redonda justo aquí. Ahora están el granero y los bueyes.

shots.direction: Moving wide: two small children chase geese along the field edge, cattle lift their heads; cloud builds over the marsh. The woman's line is called out off-screen.

lines.en: Call them in. There's cloud coming up off the marsh.
lines.cy: Galw nhw i mewn. Mae cwmwl yn codi oddi ar y gors.
lines.es: Llámalos. Viene una nube desde la marisma.

shots.direction: Moving medium shot: the woman scatters grain for the geese by the barn edge; the farmer leans on the hurdle. Both lines play as they work (no close-up).

lines.en: The geese are fat this year. One for the turn of the year.
lines.cy: Mae'r gwyddau'n dew eleni. Un ar gyfer troad y flwyddyn.
lines.es: Los gansos están gordos este año. Uno para el cambio de año.

lines.en: And one for your mother, or we'll never hear the end of it.
lines.cy: Ac un i dy fam, neu chlywn ni byth mo'i diwedd hi.
lines.es: Y uno para tu madre, o no oiremos el final.

shots.direction: Talking close-up of the farmer, laughing, wind in his hair.

lines.en: Let them run. The hill's big enough for all of us.
lines.cy: Gad iddyn nhw redeg. Mae'r bryn yn ddigon mawr i ni i gyd.
lines.es: Déjalos correr. La colina es lo bastante grande para todos.

shots.direction: Match-cut to the reading room: talking close-up of Nia, a closed excavation report under her gloved hand.

lines.en: That's a picture built from what the digs found on this hill: grain, pottery, people at work. The digs keep their own dates, and we'll read them there.
lines.cy: Darlun yw hwnna, wedi'i adeiladu o'r hyn a gafodd y cloddio ar y bryn hwn: grawn, crochenwaith, pobl wrth eu gwaith. Mae i'r cloddio ei ddyddiadau ei hun, a byddwn ni'n eu darllen nhw yno.
lines.es: Es una imagen construida con lo que hallaron las excavaciones en esta colina: grano, cerámica, gente trabajando. Las excavaciones tienen sus propias fechas, y allí las leeremos.

shots.direction: Talking close-up of the Grandson across the table.
Talking close-up of Nia closing the folder, half a smile.

lines.en: Not one, yet. Next, the graves by the church.
lines.cy: Dim un, eto. Nesaf, y beddau wrth yr eglwys.
lines.es: Ninguno, todavía. Lo siguiente, las tumbas junto a la iglesia.

shots.direction: Wordless closing hold (4 s): the hill at dusk, smoke rising, slow push-in.
